comparison: Perfect alignment on claims C98-C101 regarding model limitations and differences between mouse EAE and human MS. Both evaluations accept these as acknowledged limitations rather than fundamental flaws, with appropriate discussion of translatability concerns.

Strong overlap on background claims C1-C5, C12-C26 establishing MS clinical context and LMI-gray matter pathology relationship. Both evaluations support these as well-established background with appropriate citations, treating them as accepted context for the study.

Partial overlap on clinical background claims C1-C2, C12-C14. Both evaluations accept these as established MS facts. OpenEval groups these with additional background claims while peer review combines them with broader literature context.

Strong agreement on technical limitation claims C84-C85 regarding Visium spatial resolution. Both evaluations acknowledge this as an inherent platform constraint appropriately discussed by authors, not an execution flaw. Peer review also includes C62 (Gfap interpretation) as related to this limitation.

Minimal overlap on C62 regarding Gfap interpretation. OpenEval includes this in broader meningeal characterization (R11) as appropriately acknowledging resolution limits, while peer review groups it with technical limitations (R7).

Strong agreement on pathway analysis claims C49-C52 showing TNF, JAK-STAT, NFkB signaling near meningeal inflammation. Both evaluations support these findings as expected and well-demonstrated. Peer review explicitly confirms upregulation of complement, immune infiltration, and pathway findings.

Partial overlap on differential expression analysis claims C47-C48. Both evaluations support the DESeq2 pseudobulking approach and findings. OpenEval focuses on methodological appropriateness while peer review emphasizes biological interpretation of results.

Strong agreement on meningeal inflammation identification claims C53-C58 through unbiased clustering and MRI correlation. Both evaluations support the clustering approach and spatial inference that C11 represents meningeal inflammation without raising concerns.

Strong agreement on meningeal transcriptional characterization claims C59-C66. Both evaluations confirm identification of immune-related genes, cytokine production, and inflammatory signatures in meningeal cluster. Peer review explicitly validates these findings without critique.

Strong agreement on subclustering claims C67-C69 identifying inflamed parenchyma adjacent to LMI. Both evaluations support the approach and spatial proximity findings. Peer review confirms parenchymal clusters show glial activation and adaptive immunity.

Strong agreement on parenchymal transcriptional programs claims C70-C74. Both evaluations support gene set enrichment findings showing complement, B-cell immunity, and antigen presentation in parenchyma near meninges. Peer review explicitly confirms these canonical inflammatory signatures.

Strong agreement on trajectory analysis claims C75-C78 demonstrating gradient decay of inflammatory signals with distance from LMI. Both evaluations support this novel analytical approach. Peer review explicitly confirms descending gradients of immune pathway enrichment.

Strong agreement on RNAscope validation claims C79-C81. Both evaluations accept the orthogonal validation confirming spatial transcriptomics findings through exponential regression analysis in separate cohort. Editor emphasizes solid evidence for gradient.

Agreement on SJL EAE model rationale claims C32-C35. Both evaluations support the model choice and characterization. Peer review confirms acceptance of experimental approach without concerns about model validity.

Agreement on experimental timeline and disease course claims C36-C39, C107-C111. Both evaluations support the model characterization with behavioral data, MRI, and lesion quantification. Peer review explicitly accepts the high-field MRI approach.

Agreement on CFA control claims C40-C42, C97. Both evaluations support the demonstration that CFA alone does not induce pathology. Peer review accepts this control without raising concerns about experimental design.

Agreement on quality control claims C43-C46, C112-C115. Both evaluations support the QC metrics, filtering, and normalization approaches. Peer review confirms acceptance of data quality and spatial transcriptomics methodology.

Agreement on novelty and data availability claims C104-C105. Both evaluations acknowledge the novel approach and value to the field. Peer review emphasizes this as important study advancing understanding and providing useful resource, implicitly accepting novelty claims.

OpenEval supports claims C27-C31 summarizing prior mechanistic studies linking LMI to gray matter damage with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these background mechanism claims.

OpenEval supports claims C86-C96 discussing biological interpretation in context of oligodendrocyte biology, remyelination, and prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these discussion points.
OpenEval supports claim C121 regarding Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction method. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this statistical methodology detail.

Peer review raises uncertainty about claims C7-C10 regarding spatial resolution limitations in distinguishing meningeal versus parenchymal signals, noting immune cells do not penetrate pial surface. No corresponding OpenEval result specifically addresses these claims about potential compartment contamination.
